dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent. Tangy Dijon, sweet-tart balsamic, and herbaceous thyme pair beautifully with lean pork and asparagus.
All ingredients are properly utilized in the instructions, and no unexpected ingredients appear.
Instructions are thorough and helpful. Time ranges, halfway flips, visual doneness cues, and 'check at' prompts are all perfectly executed.
The dish aligns perfectly with the stated Mediterranean-American profile through its use of olive oil, balsamic vinegar, Dijon, and couscous.

Slicing the tenderloin into medallions and searing them is a perfect technique for lean pork, ensuring it cooks rapidly without drying out. Building the pan sauce in the same skillet efficiently captures fond.
The computed nutrition values are consistent with the quantities provided.
The title accurately describes the dish, and the intro smartly explains the culinary mechanics of the pan sauce without resorting to diet rhetoric or banned claims.
Highly appealing. It feels like a thoughtful, restaurant-style weeknight dinner that comes together easily.
The recipe delivers beautifully on both fronts: a lean protein, healthy unsaturated fat (olive oil), a pan sauce naturally free of excess saturated fat, and a measured whole-grain presence.
No added sugars are present. Despite the automated warning, 'Whole wheat couscous' clearly specifies it is a whole/intact grain, providing a quality carbohydrate base.

The recipe slightly misses the nutrient tier bounds: calories (545 > 540), carbs (57.9g > 55g), and fiber (6.7g < 7g). To perfect this, reduce the couscous from 3/4 cup dry to 1/2 cup (or 2/3 cup), and increase the asparagus to 12 oz. This will drop the carbs and calories into the target window while bumping the fiber up to the floor.
The total prep and cook time easily fits into the 30-minute promise. Using couscous, which steams passively off-heat, and quick-cooking pork medallions are smart strategies for weeknight speed.
